findings.title: A wiper ring below the rigid valve seat is not described with a purge gap in parallel with the main flow passage
findings.attack: Claim 1 requires a purge gap in parallel with the main flow passage, whose gas does not pass between the sealing face and the valve seat ([0046]). A wiper ring below the rigid valve seat ([0094]) can only see gas that has already passed that seat, so its purge gap is in series, which [0032] and [0046] exclude. [0094] and [0094a] leave the gap position, the mounting and the geometry unstated, so the combination of claims 27 and 28 with claim 1 is not disclosed (Art. 84; s.112(a)), and amending into it later would meet an added-matter objection.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventors' statement of where the third embodiment's purge gap lies and how inflation gas reaches it without passing the rigid valve seat, for example a bypass passage in the core body closed at rest by the wiper ring; if none exists in their conception, re-hang claims 27 to 29, 45, 58 and 60 from a recovery-wipe claim (narrowing, for the human to decide).

findings.title: Ranges disclosed for the first embodiment are claimed for embodiments the description expressly leaves without them
findings.attack: Through multiple dependency, claims 30 to 34 and 47 apply the pressure, over-travel and purge gap width ranges to the polymer seat ring and the wiper ring, and claim 25 via claim 19 applies the convolution amplitude to the polymer seat ring. Yet [0124] and [0125] tie those values to the first embodiment and [0093], [0104] and [0106] say no dimension is stated for the alternatives. Meanwhile [0040], [0042], [0043] and [0066] state the same ranges generally. This is an Art. 84 inconsistency, and after filing it becomes an intermediate-generalisation objection to any amendment that adds a range to claim 1.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Obtain the inventors' confirmation whether the pressure, over-travel and purge gap width ranges apply to every embodiment; if so, amend [0124] and [0125] to state them for the valve generally, keeping the seat ring dimensions tied to the seat ring; if not, restrict the dependencies of claims 19, 30 to 34 and 47 to the first-embodiment claims (narrowing of dependent claims only).

findings.title: The first embodiment's stated geometry cannot perform the claimed over-travel
findings.attack: With upper defined as towards the inflation device ([0084]), the sealing face seating on the upper edge 32 ([0030]) and the purge shoulder below the sealing face ([0029]) bearing on that upper edge during over-travel ([0111] step 706), the shoulder can reach the edge only by moving upwards against the pressure differential, and its load would then lift the ring off the locating shoulder rather than compress it. The direction of the normal stroke is stated nowhere, so the only built embodiment is not enabled on the text (Art. 83, s.112(a), UK s.14(3)), and claims 7, 14, 17, 39 and 41 recite the arrangement itself.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventors' statement of the actual arrangement (direction of the stroke, the side of the seat ring the sealing face seals on, the position of the purge shoulder and the direction of the load), align [0029], [0030], [0054], [0084], [0111] and the FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 instructions, and reword claims 7, 14 and 17 to match without narrowing.

findings.title: The purge gap cannot open where claims 16 and 40 put it, and its outlet is not described
findings.attack: The purge gap is said to lie between the outer surface 38 and the core bore 22 and to open when the seat ring expands outward ([0031], [0048]), yet the ring is held in that bore by an interference fit ([0035]); outward expansion of a ring in a bore closes a gap on its outer surface and cannot open one. No passage is described by which purge flow leaves the gap past the locating shoulder 24 into the inflatable body ([0046] says only 'may communicate'). Claim 16, through claim 15, recites the contradictory combination itself.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventors' statement of where the interference fit acts and where the outer surface is in clearance, which surfaces separate when the gap opens, and the passage past the locating shoulder; correct [0031], [0048], [0126] and claims 9, 16 and 40 if the gap actually opens by inward movement or at the upper edge.

findings.title: The breadth of deflectable element and purge gap rests on a principle plus two species with open mechanisms
findings.attack: The functional genus is supported by the principle in [0116] and by definitions that disclaim position, parts and direction ([0046], [0048]). Behind them are only the seat ring and the wiper ring, and for each of them how the purge gap opens and where it leads is unresolved on the text (F-28-1 to F-28-3). An examiner would argue that the application teaches a result without a coherent way of achieving it (Art. 84; s.112(a) written description).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Resolve F-28-1 to F-28-3, then add to [0116] any further purge gap arrangements the inventors themselves conceive; no claim narrowing.

findings.title: The figures in the package are a plan and draftsperson's instructions, not drawings, and carry internal cross-references
findings.attack: figures.md and registry.md are a figure plan and drawing instructions, not sheets, and carry internal references (CONFIRMED.md, P4/16.r1, 01 Q1, PF-1), draftsperson's notes and statements about the source material that must never be filed. Until sheets exist, no limitation draws support from a figure.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Produce the drawing sheets, remove every internal reference and note from anything filed, and check the FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 instructions against the geometry corrected under F-28-1 and F-28-2.

findings.title: The only evidence of over-travel is a snap on removal, not purge flow during inflation
findings.attack: The claims require purge flow while the inflation device supplies gas, but [0102] and [0115] evidence over-travel only by a snap on removal of the device, [0111] states that the timing within an inflation is not stated, and nothing shows that the floor pump applied the 3.5 bar differential of [0042] while inflating to 6 bar. An opponent would say that Example 1 does not show the claimed purge flow.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventors' actual observation of when over-travel occurs during pumping and whether the differential was measured; if there is none, say so expressly so that [0102] is not read as proving purge flow.

findings.title: Claim 50 adds nothing because inflatable body is defined as containing sealant
findings.attack: [0079] defines the inflatable body as one that 'contains the sealant', so claim 3 already requires sealant, claim 50 does not further limit it (s.112(d)), and claim 3 does not reach a body sold without sealant.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Amend [0079] so that sealant is an optional feature of the inflatable body ('and which in use contains sealant'), keeping [0014].

findings.title: Stainless steel is generalised from 303 stainless steel
findings.attack: Claim 13 recites 'stainless steel', but the description names only 303 stainless steel; an examiner may ask for the description to be brought into line (Art. 84).
findings.least_narrowing_action: If the inventors confirm, add 'stainless steel, for example 303 stainless steel' to [0028]; otherwise accept the objection risk.

findings.title: Path 5 has no coherent purge gap mechanism to amend into
findings.attack: The seat ring is interference-fitted in the core bore, so its outward expansion cannot open a gap on its outer surface, and no outlet past the locating shoulder 24 is described; the most distinctive structural fallback cannot be relied on as filed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Before filing, add the inventors' statement of where the interference fit acts, which surfaces separate, and the passage by which purge flow reaches the inflatable body.

findings.title: Path 9 lacks a disclosed purge gap for the wiper ring
findings.attack: A wiper ring below the rigid valve seat sees only gas that has passed the seat, so its purge gap is not the parallel path that claim 1 and [0046] require, and [0094] leaves the gap position unstated; combining claim 1 with the wiper ring would be added matter as the text stands.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventors' statement of where the third embodiment's purge gap lies and how inflation gas reaches it without passing the rigid valve seat 132; if there is none, confine Path 9 to the recovery-wipe aspect of [0011].

findings.title: Paths 2, 4, 5 and 8 have no coherent geometry to amend into
findings.attack: On the orientation of [0084], a purge shoulder below a sealing face that seals on the upper edge cannot bear on that upper edge by travel away from the seat under a pressure differential from the upper side, so every fallback built on the first embodiment inherits an Art. 83 and Art. 84 objection that cannot be cured after filing.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Before filing, add the inventors' statement of the stroke direction, the side on which the sealing face seals, and where and in which direction the purge shoulder loads the seat ring; align [0029], [0030], [0054], [0111] and the FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 instructions.

findings.title: The pressure and travel ranges are tied to the first embodiment by [0124] and [0125], defeating Path 7
findings.attack: An examiner will cite [0124] and [0125] to say that the pressure and travel ranges are disclosed only with the superelastic seat ring of the first embodiment, making their addition to claim 1 an intermediate generalisation (Art. 123(2)) unless the seat ring features are added too, which collapses Path 7 into Path 8.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Obtain the inventors' confirmation; if the ranges belong to the valve as such, restate them in [0126] and [0127] for every embodiment and confine [0124] and [0125] to the seat ring dimensions.

findings.title: No basis exists to amend the method to over-travel during a pump stroke
findings.attack: The natural method distinction, that purge flow occurs while the device is supplying gas, has no basis: [0111] expressly declines to state the timing and the only observation is a snap on removal.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If the inventors have observed when over-travel occurs during pumping, add that observation to [0111] and [0102].

findings.title: The direction of the recovery wipe is unstated, so no amendment can use it
findings.attack: [0034a] and [0055] expressly leave the direction of the sliding unstated, so Path 1 cannot be distinguished by direction or by wiping surface from references that wipe as the valve closes.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If the inventors know the direction of the sliding in the prototype, or the contacting portion of the upper edge 32, add it to [0034a] as a stated feature of the first embodiment.

findings.title: Purge gap of the first embodiment cannot open by radial expansion, and has no outlet
findings.attack: Claim 16 'opens when the seat ring expands' and claim 17 'the radial expansion opening the purge gap' place the gap between the outer surface 38 and the core bore 22, while the seat ring is interference-fitted in that bore ([0035]). Radial expansion moves the outer surface towards the bore and closes, not opens, the gap; no path from the lower end of the gap past the locating shoulder 24 into the inflatable body is described. Not enabled under US 112(a), EPC Art 83, UK s.14(3).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventors' actual gap geometry (separating surfaces, direction, outlet path) to the description and FIG. 1/2 from their sketches; only if unavailable, delete or recast claims 16, 17, 40, 41.

findings.title: Genus claims 1, 2 and 4 rest on a mechanism not coherently disclosed in any embodiment
findings.attack: Claim 1 covers any 'deflectable element' opening any 'purge gap'; [0116] calls the principle 'of general application', yet the first embodiment's gap cannot open as described and the wiper ring embodiment's gap position, mounting and thickness are 'not stated'. Full-scope enablement (Amgen v Sanofi; Regeneron v Kymab; EPC Art 83/84) is exposed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Supply the missing gap disclosure for the first embodiment and at least one stated gap topology for the wiper ring; narrowing claim 1 to a stated topology only as a fallback, for the human to decide.

findings.title: No drawings; the figure files are drafting instructions carrying internal references and damaging statements
findings.attack: The description refers to FIG. 1 to FIG. 8 but the package holds only a figure plan citing CONFIRMED.md, P1/01 and PF-1 and stating 'the disclosure does not explain how the purge gap opens', plus drawing instructions with draftsperson's notes. Missing drawings engage 35 USC 113, Rule 56 EPC and UK s.15; the statement is a sufficiency admission if filed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Produce drawing sheets for FIG. 1 to FIG. 8, matching FIG. 1 to FIG. 3 to the inventors' sketches, and keep the plan and instructions out of anything filed.

findings.title: Austenite finish temperature has no fixed measuring method
findings.attack: 'an austenite finish temperature below 5 °C' is measured by 'a thermal analysis method, for example differential scanning calorimetry, unless stated otherwise' ([0074]); Af varies by method and the prototype value is not recorded ([0128]). Unclear parameter under Art 84 (Guidelines F-IV 4.11), 112(b), s.14(5)(b).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Name one measuring method in [0074], as used by the inventors or their supplier to specify the material.

findings.title: Deflectable element construction: 112(f) placeholder in the US and displacement reading under BRI
findings.attack: 'a deflectable element' with 'opened by deflection … closed by recovery' risks 112(f) treatment limited to the seat ring 30 and wiper ring 130; without 112(f), BRI of 'deflection' may cover rigid displacement and read on spring-loaded second poppets. EPO (G 1/24) and UK read [0048]'s 'undeflected shape' into the term.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite in claim 1 'a deflectable element which is elastically deflected from an undeflected shape', and add to [0048] the structural forms as examples of the class.

findings.title: Range claims extend to alternatives for which the description says no ranges are stated
findings.attack: Claims 19, 25 (via 19) and 30 to 34 combine ranges with the polymer seat ring and the wiper ring, while [0093] and [0124] state the ranges are 'not stated' for those alternatives: Art 84 support objection now, Art 123(2) exposure on amendment, and a contrary statement quotable in the US.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Restructure dependencies so the range claims hang from the superelastic seat ring claims or claim 1 directly, not reciting the polymer or wiper combinations; or correct [0093]/[0124] if the inventors confirm the ranges apply.

findings.title: Sealant-accumulation surfaces is defined by use
findings.attack: 'along sealant-accumulation surfaces bounding the purge gap' identifies surfaces by what happens in use ([0058]); in an apparatus claim this invites a clarity objection or is given no weight, adding nothing to novelty.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite 'along surfaces bounding the purge gap' in claims 1, 2 and 4, keeping the sealant context in the description.

findings.title: The evidence that over-travel and purge flow occurred is an audible snap
findings.attack: 'Over-travel was confirmed … by an audible snap on removal of the inflation device 84' ([0102]); no pressure differential across the valve, travel or flow was measured, and the cleaning attribution is 'their statement rather than a measured result' ([0131]). Under G 2/21 the effect relied on for inventive step is weakly evidenced.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add any existing measurement of differential, travel or flow to Example 1; otherwise keep effect statements tied to the bench outcome. Nothing is to be invented.

findings.title: US multiple dependency on multiple dependent claims; claim fees in all three offices
findings.attack: Claim 8 'any one of claims 1 to 7' includes multiple dependent claim 6; claim 22 depends on multiple dependent claim 21; claims 49 and 54 depend on claim 48 and other multiple dependents. 37 CFR 1.75(c) forbids this. Sixty claims attract EPO fees beyond 15 and the higher band beyond 50, and the UK fee beyond 25.
findings.least_narrowing_action: File a US-specific claim set with single dependencies; counsel to set claim numbers per office.

findings.title: Lettered paragraph numbers
findings.attack: 37 CFR 1.52(b)(6) calls for consecutive four-digit bracketed paragraph numbers; lettered inserts are not conforming.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Renumber [0001] to [0137] consecutively (Corrections 4 to 6).

findings.title: Radial expansion of an interference-fitted seat ring cannot open a gap against its own bore, and the gap has no outlet
findings.attack: Claim 16 'opens when the seat ring expands' and claim 17 'the radial expansion opening the purge gap (60)' place the gap between the outer surface 38 and the core bore 22 in which the seat ring is interference-fitted ([0035]); expansion drives the surface into the bore and closes the gap, and no outlet past the locating shoulder 24 to the inflatable body is described.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the prototype's actual gap geometry and outlet path from the inventors' sketches or records, and draw it; delete or recast only if unavailable.

findings.title: Obvious over US20080188352A1 in view of US3417778A; under broadest reasonable interpretation, possible anticipation
findings.attack: Ref. 4 [25], [26], [31], [37], [38]: ball 3 stroke limited by shuttle 4 of poppet 2; at a higher second pressure the poppet and ball travel further, opening a parallel orifice at seat 11 that recloses as pressure falls. The difference is rigid displacement instead of deflection; ref. 3 claim 1 supplies a resilient seat element flexed 'radially outwardly'. Under BRI 'deflects' may mean displaces, exposing claim 1 to anticipation by ref. 4.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite in claim 1 that the deflectable element is 'elastically deflected from an undeflected shape' and that the purge gap is 'bounded at least in part by a surface of the deflectable element' ([0046], [0048]); no described embodiment is lost.

findings.title: The directions of seat, sealing face, purge shoulder and spring cannot all be true at once
findings.attack: With 'upper' towards the inflation device ([0084]), a valve member opening downward cannot lift from an upward-facing 'upper edge (32)' seat; a spring 'acting under the valve member' ([0033]) pushes it away from such a seat; and a purge shoulder 'below the sealing face' moves away from, not onto, the upper edge during further travel. The first embodiment cannot be reconstructed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Correct the orientation words to the inventors' actual construction and state the direction of the normal stroke relative to the upper edge; claims 7, 14, 17, 39, 41 follow.

findings.title: The wiper-ring purge gap lies below the rigid valve seat, so it is in series with the main flow passage, not in parallel
findings.attack: Claim 28 'positioned below the rigid valve seat (132), towards the inflatable body' means gas reaching the wiper-ring gap has already passed between the sealing face and the rigid seat, i.e. in series, which [0046] excludes from 'purge gap'; no bypass is described.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a described purge gap inlet that bypasses the rigid valve seat if conceived; otherwise delete the wiper-ring claims or reframe that embodiment on the recovery wipe alone.

findings.title: Af parameter with an open measuring method
findings.attack: 'an austenite finish temperature below 5 °C' measured by 'a thermal analysis method, for example differential scanning calorimetry' leaves the boundary method-dependent; the prototype Af is not recorded.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Name the measuring method the inventors used.

findings.title: Pressure thresholds are claimed with no measuring condition
findings.attack: 'the over-travel threshold is from 2.5 bar to 5.0 bar' is a differential on the valve member whose value under flow depends on flow rate and passage geometry; [0039] fixes the quantity but not the condition (static or flowing).
findings.least_narrowing_action: State in [0039] the condition under which the values are determined, as the inventors actually set them.

findings.title: The recovery wipe is known in kind from US4050473A and US4236547A
findings.attack: Ref. 5 [13] (flexible disk wiping the seat as it moves past) and ref. 6 [6] (cutting edge cleaning the skirt on closing) show wiping sealing surfaces by sliding contact on closing; adding it to claim 1 is an aggregation absent shown synergy, and [0103], [0131] say contributions were not isolated.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If the inventors can state it, add how the element's recovery produces the sliding (direction, moving surfaces) in the first embodiment.

findings.title: The seat ring fallbacks add features known from US3417778A
findings.attack: Ref. 3 [14]-[15]: 'a tubular sleeve-like element of resilient material … the sole valve seat and being radially expandable', flexed 'radially outwardly' by the valve member; claims 9, 11 and 14 add nothing beyond one document and are weak fallbacks.
findings.least_narrowing_action: No amendment now; treat claims 6, 17 and 20 as the real fallback rungs and consider combining claim 14 with claim 17.

findings.title: The technical effect rests on an audible snap and the inventors' attribution
findings.attack: 'Over-travel was confirmed … by an audible snap on removal of the inflation device 84' ([0102]); no differential, travel or flow was measured and the cleaning attribution is 'their statement rather than a measured result' ([0131]), inviting reformulation of the problem as an alternative two-stage valve.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add any existing measurement; otherwise keep statements tied to the bench outcome. Nothing is to be invented.

findings.title: Undeflected at rest, although the seating load bears on the upper edge that converts axial load into expansion
findings.attack: Claim 1(a) 'the deflectable element is undeflected' at rest, yet the sealing face seats on the upper edge under the biasing member and the inflatable body's pressure, and by [0030] any axial load on the upper edge is converted into radial expansion; 'undeflected' has no reference condition.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Define 'undeflected' in [0048] as the shape in which the purge gap is closed whatever seating load acts, and rely on 'the purge gap is closed' as the operative limitation.

findings.title: US multiple dependent claims depend on other multiple dependent claims
findings.attack: Claim 8 'The valve of any one of claims 1 to 7' refers to claim 6 'claim 1 or claim 5', itself multiple dependent; the same pattern appears in claims 17, 30, 48, 54 and many others. This is improper under 35 U.S.C. 112(e) and 37 CFR 1.75(c); such claims are objected to and not examined, and multiple-dependency fees apply.
findings.least_narrowing_action: File a US-specific claim set with single dependencies chosen by counsel; keep the EPO/UK set (Correction 2 shows claim 8 as an example).

findings.title: According to the inventors attributions and has been considered in the specification
findings.attack: 'each is stated here as the inventors state it', 'According to the inventors' and 'Hard-anodised aluminium has been considered' distance the applicant from its own teaching and are read as unsupported assertions or non-disclosure.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State teachings positively and keep the observed/expected distinction through the Examples.

findings.title: Product-by-process with process parameters
findings.attack: Claim 24 defines the seat ring by laser cutting, shape-setting at 500 °C for 10 minutes, quenching and electropolishing; EPO requires product novelty per se and US scope is limited to the process.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Keep as a low-value rung or add a method-of-making claim supported by [0108] and FIG. 6.

findings.title: The method recites events and parts' behaviour rather than steps
findings.attack: Claim 4 'the valve member making a normal stroke', 'the pressure differential falling', 'the deflectable element recovering' are apparatus responses, not acts, inviting a clarity objection on category and actor.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recast as acts (applying, increasing above the threshold, ceasing to apply) with the valve's responses as whereby clauses.

findings.title: "Undeflected" in ranges (a) and (b) is an absolute limitation avoided by a light preload
findings.attack: Claims 1 and 2 require that in (a) 'the deflectable element is undeflected' and in (b) it 'remains undeflected'; claim 4 requires 'while the deflectable element remains undeflected'. A competitor preloads the purge shoulder lightly on the element, so it is always slightly deflected while the purge gap stays closed until the threshold; the product is literally outside all independent claims and the patentee must prove zero deflection against micron-level evidence.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete the 'undeflected' statements from (a) and (b) of claims 1 and 2 and from claim 4, keeping 'the purge gap is closed / remains closed', supported separately by [0044], [0046] and [0134]; keep 'undeflected' as a dependent fallback. Moderate EPO intermediate-generalisation risk because [0009] and [0041] state both together.

findings.title: Purge gap limited to a second parallel path; enlarging the seat gap on over-travel avoids claims 1, 2 and 4
findings.attack: Claims 1 and 2 require 'a purge gap (60), which is a second path for inflation gas ... in parallel with the main flow passage' and [0046] says purge gas 'does not pass between the sealing face and the valve seat'. A core whose over-travel flexes the seat element to widen the seat annulus, and which wipes the sealing face on recovery, has no second path and avoids every independent claim while keeping both cleaning actions of [0010]. The recovery wipe is claimed only in dependent claims hanging on the purge gap.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent valve and valve-core claim to the recovery-wipe aspect of [0011] (normal stroke, over-travel above a higher threshold deflecting the deflectable element, and recovery with the deflectable element sliding across the sealing face), with no purge-gap limitation; supported by [0011], [0034], [0034a], [0055], [0117]. A new claim, not a narrowing; counsel to weigh proximity to US4050473A and US4236547A.

findings.title: Deflection only by the valve member's over-travel; deflection by gas pressure or by the pump head avoids the claims
findings.attack: Claims 1 and 2 require 'the over-travel of the valve member deflects the deflectable element'. A resilient element that yields directly to gas pressure above a threshold, or a pump-head pin that opens the purge path, avoids the claims. The package discloses only valve-member-driven deflection ([0116]); broadening towards pressure-driven deflection runs towards US3417778A claim 1 ('radially expandable under fluid pressure').
findings.least_narrowing_action: None within the present text. If the inventors have conceived pressure-driven or pump-actuated opening, disclose it as a further embodiment and assess it against US3417778A before claiming; otherwise record as accepted residual scope. No narrowing proposed.

findings.title: Method claim 4 is performed by the rider, so it reaches a competitor only through indirect infringement
findings.attack: Claim 4 is performed 'in one inflation of the inflatable body through the valve by an inflation device (84): applying, by the inflation device, a pressure differential'. The rider performs it, and only when the pump exceeds the threshold ([0113]: no statement that every inflation device reaches it). Against a core maker the claim depends on inducement or contributory infringement (US) or s.60(2)-type supply of means (UK, EPC states), each needing knowledge or intent and proof of a user's inflation.
findings.least_narrowing_action: No change to claim 4; keep apparatus claims 1, 2, 3 and 48 as the enforcement claims and let counsel decide whether the method claim is worth its place.

findings.title: Purge flow and purge-gap closure are provable only by a bench test the description does not describe
findings.attack: Claims 1 and 2 require 'purge flow (64) of the inflation gas passes through the purge gap' and 'the purge gap closes'. [0046] defines closed as 'does not admit purge flow' and [0132a] admits 'no measurement herein isolates the purge gap'. A defendant's expert argues either no measurable purge flow or leakage at rest; the patentee has no disclosed test to point to, and the behaviour is invisible outside an inflation above threshold.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to the description the test by which purge flow through the purge gap and its closure at rest are identified on a valve core, with its acceptance criterion, as supplied by the inventors. Added disclosure, no claim change.

findings.title: Recovery-wipe dependent claims are hard to prove on a commercial product
findings.attack: Claims 5, 35 and 52 require that 'the deflectable element slides across the sealing face (42)'. Relative sliding of two moving parts inside a closed core, direction unstated ([0034a], [0055]), needs high-speed imaging or wear analysis to prove; a defendant argues the parts separate before sliding.
findings.least_narrowing_action: No claim change. If F-33-1 is taken up, state in the description the observable evidence of the recovery wipe relied on; only the audible snap of [0102] and [0115] is in the package now.

findings.title: Method claim 4 scores 2 for detectability and 2 for evidentiary ease
findings.attack: Claim 4 is performed 'in one inflation of the inflatable body through the valve by an inflation device (84): applying, by the inflation device, a pressure differential across the valve', inside a closed valve during a user's inflation, and only if the pump exceeds the threshold, which [0113] says is not assured. It cannot be detected from a product on sale, is provable only by end-user evidence plus knowledge or intent, and adds no validity strength over claim 1.
findings.least_narrowing_action: No change; counsel to decide whether the claim earns its place against its fee and against using the slot for the recovery-wipe independent claim of F-33-1. Same root cause as F-33-3.

findings.title: No drawings exist; the purge gap is drawn "schematically" with no inlet or outlet
findings.attack: figures.md records that the inventors' sketches 'exist by name only; no image has been seen' and instructs 'draw no inlet or outlet feature' for the purge gap; [0026] says it is shown schematically. There are no drawings, drawings cannot be added after filing without added-matter exposure, and figures.md contains internal working references and draftsperson's notes that are not filing text.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Obtain the inventors' sketches and prepare formal drawings of FIG. 1 to FIG. 8, with FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 showing the actual purge-gap region and flow path at rest and in over-travel; file drawings and a brief description, not the figure plan.

findings.title: The first embodiment's purge gap opens "when the seat ring 30 expands" into the bore that holds it by interference
findings.attack: [0031] and claims 16 and 40 say the purge gap 'is formed between the outer surface 38 of the seat ring 30 and the core bore 22 ... and opens when the seat ring 30 expands', while [0035] holds the seat ring in that bore by an interference fit. Outward radial expansion drives the outer surface into the bore; the text does not say how a gap opens between them, where the fit acts, or how gas enters and leaves the gap. The only built embodiment's mechanism is not taught: insufficiency (Art. 83, s.14(3)) and enablement (112(a)) exposure.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventors' description of the first embodiment's purge-gap geometry: the region held by the interference fit, the region forming the purge gap, which surface moves from which in over-travel, and the gas path in and out, with the sketch. Correct claims 16 and 40 only if the added text shows a different location.

findings.title: Behaviour on manual depression of the valve member and with the lock nut is not stated
findings.attack: [0114] makes no statement whether manual depression of the valve member 'produces over-travel or purge flow 64' or whether the lock nut prevents over-travel, though every Example 1 cycle ended in full deflation through the valve ([0099]). This bears on fatigue, the rest-state seal and whether a 'press to purge' competitor practises the invention.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State what the inventors observed on deflating the prototype by pressing the valve member, and whether the lock nut limits valve-member travel.

findings.title: No dimensions for the polymer seat ring or the wiper ring
findings.attack: [0093] and [0094a] state that the polymer seat ring dimensions and the wiper ring thickness, mounting and contacting portion are not stated. The second and third embodiments are prophetic with material only; an opponent argues undue experimentation for the claims directed to them.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the dimensions or ranges the inventors contemplate for the polymer seat ring and the wiper ring, and the wiper ring's mounting in the core body.

findings.title: No range is stated for the normal stroke
findings.attack: [0126]: 'The normal stroke is 0.6 mm in the prototype; no range is stated for it', while claim 31 measures over-travel 'beyond the end of the normal stroke'. An opponent argues the three-range behaviour is disclosed only at 0.6 mm; no fallback on stroke exists.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the normal-stroke range the inventors believe would work, with endpoints disclosed individually as in [0085].

findings.title: Only the Presta pattern is disclosed; no Schrader or other valve-standard embodiment
findings.attack: Every embodiment is Presta ([0027]) although [0070] says the valve core term 'does not itself import any thread form or valve standard'. A competitor's Schrader-pattern purging core will be argued outside what is disclosed, and a later claim to a Schrader core would lack basis.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a paragraph on Schrader-pattern and other valve-standard cores, with any structural adaptation the inventors contemplate, and the further sealant-filled inflatable bodies they contemplate.

findings.title: The geometry of the recovery wipe is not stated
findings.attack: [0034a]: 'The direction of that sliding relative to the axis of the valve 92 is not stated herein'. The recovery wipe is one of the two cleaning actions and the basis of the independent claim proposed in F-33-1, but the text does not say how the upper edge stays in sliding contact with the conical sealing face while the ring contracts and the valve member returns.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventors' account of the relative motion in the recovery wipe (direction, sequence, contact path on the sealing face) and, for the wiper ring, the contacting portion.

findings.title: Spring rates and the effective area of the valve member are not stated
findings.attack: [0063] describes 'a soft first stage ... and a stiffer second stage' only by the pressures they set; no spring rate, preload or effective area is stated, so the spring cannot be derived from 1.0 bar and 3.5 bar and no spring fallback has basis.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the prototype's first- and second-stage spring rates or loads and the effective area on which the pressure differential acts.

findings.title: The thermal purge variant is disclosed without a mechanism
findings.attack: [0096] states that warming 'opens the purge gap without an inflation device' without saying how a two-way shape-memory seat ring deflects to do so, and records that no data exist and the inventors are undecided. It supports no claim and teaches competitors a direction.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventors' account of the mechanism if the variant is kept; otherwise counsel and the human decide whether it stays as a recorded variant. Deletion not proposed.

findings.title: Claim 4: distinguishing method steps are conditional, so the method reads on any inflation of any valve
findings.attack: Under BRI (Ex parte Schulhauser; MPEP 2111.04 II) the steps introduced by 'when the pressure differential exceeds an opening pressure' and 'when the pressure differential exceeds an over-travel threshold' need not be performed. Only 'applying, by the inflation device, a pressure differential across the valve' is required, which any tyre-valve inflation (e.g. reference 1, US11338632B2) meets. This is a credible US anticipation rejection that needs an amendment.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite the rise of the pressure differential above the opening pressure and then above the over-travel threshold as a positive step, and recast the two 'when' clauses as consequences of it ('as the pressure differential exceeds ...'). Scope is unchanged; see Corrections 1 to 3.

findings.title: 'Deflectable element' invites a US means-plus-function construction
findings.attack: 'a deflectable element', characterised by 'opened by deflection of the deflectable element and closed by recovery', pairs a nonce word ('element', MPEP 2181) with function. Under Williamson v. Citrix, 35 U.S.C. 112(f) may confine it to the seat ring 30, the wiper ring 130 and equivalents. The disclaimer in [0088] does not bind a court.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Keep the term, with the structure the description already gives ([0043], [0046], [0054]). Counsel may add 'elastically' before 'deflectable element' in the US set. No change is proposed now.

findings.title: 'Remains undeflected' in range (b) is an unnecessary, measurable limitation
findings.attack: Claim 1(b) 'the deflectable element remains undeflected and the purge gap remains closed' (and claims 2(b) and 4) lets a competitor add slight elastic deflection during the normal stroke (a preload contact, or seat compression) that does not open the purge gap, and argue non-infringement. [0048] ties 'undeflected shape' to closure of the purge gap, but that definition is circular and a court may apply the ordinary meaning.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete 'the deflectable element remains undeflected and' from range (b) of claims 1 and 2, and the parallel phrase from claim 4. Keep the purge-gap-closed limitation and range (a). This slightly broadens the claims (support [0031], [0041], [0046]). Scope decision for P5 and counsel.

findings.title: Claims 25 and 44 include a self-contradictory superelastic-and-polymer branch
findings.attack: Claim 25 'wherein the seat ring (30) is a polymer seat ring' reaches claim 10 'the deflectable element is of a superelastic alloy' via claims 14, 12 and 10. Claim 44 reaches claim 38 via claim 39. Those branches require one seat ring to be both, contrary to [0097], and are unclear under EPC Art. 84.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Exclude the contradictory branch with 'as dependent directly or indirectly on ...' (Corrections 13 and 14). Every consistent combination is kept.

findings.title: Claims 8-12 and 30-33 depend on claims of another category
findings.attack: 'The valve of any one of claims 1 to 7' (and the like in claims 9-12, 30-33) takes in claim 2 (valve core), claim 3 (inflatable body) and claim 4 (method), so 'the valve of claim 2/3/4' has no clear referent. This is an EPC Art. 84 / UK s.14(5)(b) clarity objection and a US cross-category dependency objection.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Change each range to 'claim 1 or any one of claims 5 to N' (Corrections 4 to 12). No intended combination is lost.

findings.title: Claim 24 is a product-by-process fallback of little value
findings.attack: 'made by laser cutting (602) ..., shape-setting (604) ... at a temperature of 500 °C for a period of 10 minutes, water quenching (606) and electropolishing (608)' is read as the product for novelty, so it adds nothing over claim 20 unless the route leaves a structural signature, and none is stated. In US infringement it is limited to the process (Abbott v. Sandoz), which is avoided by changing a parameter.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Keep it as a fallback, or replace it with a method-of-making claim with the values in dependants (support [0108], FIG. 6). Counsel's choice.

findings.title: Claim 7: 'below' has no reference direction in the claim
findings.attack: 'an annular step of the valve member (40) below the sealing face (42)' depends on the orientation convention of [0084]. Read alone, the claim is orientation-dependent.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Replace 'below the sealing face (42)' with 'on the side of the sealing face (42) towards the inflatable body (80)' (Correction 15).

findings.title: Example 1 is internally impossible as written (test dates and C-2 failure row)
findings.attack: [0099] states forty inflation cycles each with 'a hold of 24 hours', yet 'The test ran from 2026-08-12 to 2026-08-20' (eight days for at least forty days of holds). Table 1 row C-2 records 0.7 bar leak-down at last measured cycle 11 but failure at cycle 12, against the 0.5 bar criterion of [0100]. The only actual example is impeachable, and the error is not correctable after filing because the correct values are not derivable from the text (EPC Rule 139).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Obtain the actual test record from the inventor and correct the dates or hold duration in [0099], [0100] and [0059], and the C-2 row and column headings of Table 1. No claim change.

findings.title: 'The valves described herein' statements exclude viable embodiments (added valve, one moving part, whole mechanism in the core)
findings.attack: [0007] 'by the action of one moving part, with no tool, no action by the rider, no stored gas and no valve additional to the valve member' and [0017] 'the whole mechanism is contained in the valve core' are general statements about the invention. They support a US disavowal argument by a competitor who adds a series one-way valve, conflict with claim 1 (no valve core required) and with [0122] (clamping by the valve stem), and are inaccurate on the description's own terms (the deflectable element and biasing member move).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recast them as statements about the embodiments described and drop 'one moving part' (Corrections 1 and 4).

findings.title: Definitions of 'sealing face' and 'inflatable body' import dependent-claim features into independent claims
findings.attack: [0050] defines 'sealing face' as the surface 'across which the deflectable element slides in the recovery wipe', which by US lexicography imports claim 5 into claims 1, 2 and 4. [0079] defines 'inflatable body' as one that 'contains the sealant', which imports claim 50 into claim 3 and lets a tube supplied dry escape direct infringement.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Limit each definition to what the term is: make the recovery wipe a conditional sentence and the sealant a condition of use (Corrections 5 and 6).

findings.title: Ranges disclaimed for the polymer seat ring and wiper ring, yet claims 30-34 and 47 depend on those embodiments
findings.attack: [0093] 'are not stated for the polymer seat ring', [0106] 'No dimension is stated for the wiper ring 130' and [0124] 'not stated for the alternatives' deny the ranges for combinations that claims 30-34 (through claims 25-29) and 47 (through claims 44-45) expressly claim. This draws an EPC Art. 84 / 35 U.S.C. 112(a) inconsistency objection, and an opponent will cite the description's own denial.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Ask the inventor whether the pressure, over-travel and purge gap width ranges apply to those embodiments. If yes, amend [0093], [0106], [0124] and [0125]. If no, restrict the dependencies of claims 30-34 and 47 (narrowing, which loses only those combinations).

findings.title: The summary states a sealant-film removal effect that the only data partly contradict
findings.attack: [0007] 'The valves described herein remove sealant film that has already formed' and [0017] 'purge themselves of sealant film' are contradicted by [0103] 'Cured sealant film was present on the outer surface 38 of each seat ring 30 in the region of the purge gap 60', which is a sealant-accumulation surface. An EPO examiner will reformulate the problem as a less ambitious one, and a litigant will attack purge flow as the mechanism.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recast [0007] and [0017] to state the action (purge flow along the sealant-accumulation surfaces; recovery wipe) and the observation of Example 1, not an unqualified removal result (Corrections 1 and 2).

findings.title: 'Operates as a conventional valve' characterises the claimed normal-stroke behaviour as known
findings.attack: 'in this range the valve operates as a conventional valve' and its variants let an examiner cite the applicant's own words for ranges (a) and (b) and the main flow passage without a reference. The practical effect is small because reference 1 already shows this.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Replace with 'operates without purge flow' (Corrections 3 and 7 to 10).

findings.title: Background pinpoints use database paragraph indices, not the documents' own numbering
findings.attack: 'at paragraph [13] and at paragraph [6] respectively' (US4050473A, US4236547A), 'at paragraphs [22] and [26]' (US3570510A) and 'at paragraph [10]' (US6053992A) cite paragraphs that do not exist in grants printed with column and line numbering. '[26]' is not the [00NN] form of US20080188352A1. This misstates where the art is found.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Drop the pinpoints and keep the characterisations (Corrections 12 to 17). Counsel can add column-and-line pinpoints from the official documents.

findings.title: The description contradicts itself on the core body material of the tested prototype
findings.attack: [0028] 'The core body 20 is turned from free-machining brass CW614N in the prototype', with 'prototype' defined in [0090] as the tested units, conflicts with [0132] 'the material of the core body 20 of the valve cores 90 tested in Example 1 ... not recorded herein'. This invites an attack on the accuracy of the record.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Ask the inventor, then either delete the words from [0132] or detach CW614N from the tested units in [0028] and [0067].

findings.title: The method summary in [0015] is narrower than claim 4
findings.attack: [0015] 'and removing the inflation device, so that the pressure differential falls' is narrower than claim 4 'ceases to apply pressure to the valve or is removed from it'. Read as 'the invention', it could confine claim 4 to removal of the device.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Align [0015] with claim 4 and [0039] (Correction 11).

findings.title: No drawing sheets exist, though the description relies on eight figures
findings.attack: [0018]-[0025] describe FIG. 1 to FIG. 8, but the package holds only a figure plan and drawing instructions, pending the inventors' sketches. 35 U.S.C. 113 requires drawings here; EPC Rule 56 and UK s.15(5) delete the references or re-date the application when drawings are missing.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Prepare FIG. 1 to FIG. 8 from the registry.md instructions, reconciled with FIG-1.png and FIG-2.png, and file them with the description.

findings.title: 'Inflation gas' carries no reference sign (66) in claims 1, 2 and 4
findings.attack: 'along which inflation gas passes the valve seat' (claims 1 and 2) and 'inflation gas from the inflation device' (claim 4) omit the sign 66 shown in FIG. 2, although every other numbered component carries its sign (EPC Rule 43(7)).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add '(66)' at the first mention in each independent claim (Corrections 11 to 13).

findings.title: Claimed tubeless tyre set-up and outward-deflected wiper ring are not shown in any figure
findings.attack: Claim 51 'a tubeless tyre set-up' and claims 28 and 45 'deflected outward by the purge shoulder (44)' are not drawn: FIG. 8 shows only an inner tube, and FIG. 3 shows the wiper ring 130 only undeflected. This is contrary to 37 CFR 1.83(a).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the deflected wiper ring in broken line to FIG. 3 and a labelled box for the tubeless tyre set-up to FIG. 8 (Corrections 14 and 15).

findings.title: Claims 57 to 60 are not grouped with the claims they depend on
findings.attack: '57. The valve of claim 20', '58. The valve of any one of claims 27 to 29', '59. The valve core of claim 42' and '60. The valve core of claim 45' follow method claims 52-56, contrary to EPC Rule 43(4).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Move them after claims 24, 29, 43 and 45 respectively and renumber (Correction 10).

findings.title: FIG. 4A and FIG. 4B each combine two different views
findings.attack: [0021] 'FIG. 4A shows, in axial section and in end view' puts two different views under one figure number, contrary to 37 CFR 1.84(u)(1) and EPC Rule 46(2)(h).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Drop the end views, which add only D, already shown in section (Corrections 7 to 9); or renumber the views as FIG. 4A to 4D.

findings.title: No abstract in the package
findings.attack: An abstract is required under 37 CFR 1.72(b) (at most 150 words), EPC Art. 78(1)(e) and Rule 47, and UK s.14(2)(c); none is in the package.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Write an abstract summarising claim 1 with the FIG. 2 reference signs.

findings.title: The claims have no heading
findings.attack: claims.md begins '1. A valve (92) for an inflatable body (80)' with no heading; 37 CFR 1.75(h) and MPEP 608.01(m) expect claims on a separate sheet under a heading, as do the EPO and the UK IPO.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add 'CLAIMS' above claim 1 (Correction 16).
